newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit hits 17-month high.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit hits 17-month high.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit hit a 17-month high against the U.S. dollar in early Monday trade as U.S. and Japanese funds continued to pile in on bullish sentiment for the stock market and overall economy.
Profit-taking pushed the ringgit down from a high of 2.4690 to around 2.4710/20 against the dollar at 0430 GMT. On August 15, 1995, the ringgit hit a high of 2.4620.
Dealers said the ringgit's rise was supported by stop-loss dollar sales around the 2.4780/90 area and the apparent absence of Bank Negara Malaysia.
They said buying was hectic with Singapore and Kuala Lumpur-based players joining the ringgit buying spree in late morning trading.
"Once the offshore banks saw Bank Negara was not likely to come in, they pushed higher, which triggered stop-losses," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.

A Singapore-based U.S. bank dealer said the ringgit looked set to head towards 2.4500 against the dollar in the medium term. "Technically, the market is looking at 2.4500, which I think is a high possibility," he said.
"If the market doesn't see Negara checking, maybe they'll push (dollar/ringgit) down again later on," he added.
But research firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore said fears of central bank intervention could spur players to take profit.
"Although ringgit gains should be capped around the psychological 2.4700 resistance, the bias is still for a stronger ringgit in the medium-term," I.D.E.A. said in its daily report.
Further south, the Singapore dollar maintained its poise as the ringgit's bull run did not translate into much ringgit/Sing buying, dealers said.
"It's more straight dollar/ringgit," said the U.S. bank dealer. He said the U.S. dollar's topside looked confined to S$1.4050 as local banks had shown selling interest from S$1.4060.
In Indonesia, the rupiah continued to be buoyed by offshore speculation of a band widening despite its failure to materialise last week.
The central bank governor shrugged off the market talk last week by saying monetary policy would be kept flexible and adjusted when necessary but he declined to say when.
However, the governor also said the rupiah exchange rate would be kept at a realistic level without anti-export bias.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,363.75/64.25 at 0430 GMT compared with an opening of 2,363.75/64.10.

Dealers said swap premiums tumbled across the board on anticipation of ample rupiah supply on Tuesday following the central bank's heavy dollar purchases last Friday, when the spot rate fell below its intervention band floor.
The Thai baht slid in the face of the dollar's gains versus the yen, but dealers said its fall was cushioned by some dollar/baht selling due to higher short-term domestic interest rates.
The baht was quoted at 25.630-25.635 to the dollar at 0430 GMT against 25.610-25.626 late on Friday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.65, unchanged from Friday.
"The dollar was traded quite low against the central bank's fixing this morning. The high (short-term) interest rates triggered some selling of the dollar for baht," said a Bangkok dealer.

Dealers said liquidity was tightening ahead of monthly value-added tax payments. The central bank's decision to increase the bond auction last Friday to $200 million from the $80 million previously planned also squeezed liquidity.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
